n: Loving correction is the same as loving knowledge. Hating correction is acting like an animal without reason.

f.g: brutish = stupid, like a dumb animal.

n: The Lord shows favor to good people but condemns those who scheme.
Wickedness can’t give anyone a secure place, but the righteous are rooted firmly like a deep-rooted tree.

f.w: the root of the righteous shall not be moved

n: A woman of strong character brings honor to her husband like a crown; one who shames him is like a disease eating his bones.

f.g: Hebrew ʾeshet ḥayil—a woman of strength, worth, and capability.

n: The plans of the righteous are just; the advice of the wicked is deceptive.
The words of the wicked set deadly ambushes, but the speech of the upright rescues people.
The wicked are overthrown and gone, but the house of the righteous stands firm.

f.w: the house of the righteous shall stand

n: People are praised for good sense; those with twisted minds are despised.
Better to be an ordinary person who has a servant (that is, modest means) than to put on airs while having no food.

f.g: Plays the great man; pretends to be important.

n: Righteous people even care for the needs of their animals. Kindness reaches all creatures, while the wicked’s “kindness” is cruel.

f.w: regardeth the life of his beast

n: Working your land brings plenty of food, but chasing worthless pursuits shows a lack of sense.
The wicked covet what evil men catch, but the root of the righteous bears real fruit.

f.g: Possibly “the loot” or “stronghold” of evil men; the Hebrew is difficult.

n: Evil people are trapped by their own sinful talk, but the righteous escape trouble.
Good words and good work both bring good returns. People reap what their mouths and hands produce.

f.w: the recompence of a man's hands

n: Fools think they are always right; wise people listen to advice.
A fool shows irritation immediately, but a sensible person overlooks an insult.

f.g: Ignores an insult; doesn’t make a scene.

n: Telling the truth brings justice; a false witness spreads deceit.
Careless words can stab like a sword, but the words of the wise heal.
Truth lasts forever; a lie lasts only a moment.

f.w: The lip of truth shall be established for ever

n: Deceit fills the hearts of those who plot evil, but those who promote peace have joy.
A general principle: no lasting harm overtakes the righteous, while the wicked are full of trouble. Scripture elsewhere recognizes that the righteous still suffer in this life.

f.w: There shall no evil happen to the just

n: The Lord detests lying lips but delights in people who are trustworthy.

f.w: Lying lips are abomination to the LORD

n: A sensible person doesn’t show off what he knows, but fools broadcast their foolishness.
Diligent people end up leading; lazy people end up in forced labor.

f.g: Subject to forced labor or payments to others.

n: Anxiety weighs a person down, but a kind word lifts them up. Encouragement is a real gift.

f.w: a good word maketh it glad

n: The righteous are careful guides to their neighbors; the way of the wicked leads them astray.

f.w: is more excellent than his neighbour
f.g: Possibly “guides his neighbor” or “searches out his friends”; the Hebrew is uncertain.

n: A lazy hunter doesn’t even bother to cook what he caught; but diligence is a precious possession.

f.w: roasteth not that which he took in hunting

n: The road of righteousness leads to life—and on that path is no death. Some see here an early hint of immortality.
